compactRecord.rs: Highest Tuscan-Emilian Apennine pass with pleasant mountain scenery, but the road is largely unpaved, the Modena side is closed to traffic, the summit is a bare saddle, and it has virtually no international recognition beyond local hikers and gravel cyclists.
compactRecord.td: Foce a Giovo (1,667 m) is the highest pass of the Tuscan-Emilian Apennines, historically called the 'Via Ducale' after its 1819 ducal construction. The Tuscan approach ends in 5 km of gravel; the Modena side is fully unpaved and closed to vehicles, making this an adventure-gravel destination with modest summit facilities.

The summit hosts the iconic twin 18th-century pyramids marking the old Tuscany–Modena border, a ski resort village, and a botanical garden — more character than most Italian Apennine passes, though the scenery is forested rather than dramatic alpine.

compactRecord.td: Historically rich Apennine crossing at 1,041 m, a key waypoint on the Via Francigena pilgrimage route since the 8th century. The summit holds a church and traditional facilities amid pleasant forested hills, though drama-seekers will find the landscape tame and most through-traffic uses the A15 tunnel below.
